Fleeting

FLEE-ting -- two syllables, stress on the first syllable, FLEE. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Fleeting is lasting a very short time.

A fleeting smile crossed the guard's face before he waved them through the gate.

Worked Example

The photographer has crouched by the pond since dawn, camera aimed at a bare branch. Four hours pass. Then the kingfisher drops -- a blue flash, a splash, a fish -- and is gone. The whole dive took half a second, and she got exactly one frame of it.

The kingfisher's dive was fleeting: lasting a very short time, over almost before it registered. Fleeting is about speed -- the moment races past, and you catch it or you miss it. A fleeting glance, a fleeting thought, a fleeting chance: all gone in a blink.

How Fleeting Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

momentary

momentary: lasting only a moment

brief

brief: short in duration

passing

passing: going by quickly

Antonyms

lasting

lasting: continuing for a long time

prolonged

prolonged: stretched out longer than usual

How Strong Is It? — brief → fleeting → momentary

brief vs. fleeting

brief vs. fleeting: Brief just measures the clock -- a brief meeting might still be scheduled and calm -- while fleeting adds motion: the moment rushes past and is gone before you can hold it.

momentary vs. fleeting

momentary vs. fleeting: Momentary is the strongest compression, shrinking something to a single moment, but it is neutral about how the moment felt; fleeting keeps the ache of speed -- a fleeting glimpse is one you nearly missed and cannot get back.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — fleet

Root — fleet: to float, to flow or glide swiftly (from Old English fleotan -- the same root as fleet, meaning fast)

Suffix — -ing

Suffix — -ing: adjective-forming: in the act of (Old English)

Put it together

Put it together: Fleet ('to glide swiftly', from Old English fleotan -- the root that also gives fleet, meaning fast) + -ing spell fleeting: a fleeting moment is literally one gliding swiftly past you, like a leaf on a stream -- visible, moving, and impossible to hold.

Use the root in a new word: fleet-footed

Use the root in a new word: fleet-footed: The fleet-footed messenger crossed the whole valley before noon.

Root Check

Word Choice

Fleeting attaches to quick, vivid moments: a fleeting glance, a fleeting smile, fleeting joy, a fleeting opportunity. Its emphasis is the speed of the passing. Keep it apart from its unit-mate transient, which stresses impermanence -- transient workers stay for a season; a fleeting glimpse is over in a second. If you could measure it with a stopwatch, it is fleeting; if with a calendar, it is transient.
